sources.citation: The Daly Languages site (Ian Green & Rachel Nordlinger 2022), Resources and Corpus pages.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; bibliography lists 'Harvey, Mark. 1989. A Sketch Grammar of Kamu. Unpublished manuscript. Held at AIATSIS', 'Harvey, Mark. 1989. Kamu Dictionary', Harvey 2003 chapters, Tryon 1968/1974, and Zandvoort 1999 Matngele grammar; Green corpus item IG9-019 is a copy of Harvey's Kamu audio (speaker O'Brien). Typology page is a placeholder.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. The evolution of verb systems in the Eastern Daly language family, pp. 159-184; and The evolution of object enclitic paradigms in the Eastern Daly language family, pp. 185-201. In N. Evans (ed.), The Non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia. Pacific Linguistics 552.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; morphological/historical chapters (Kamu data from last speaker Elsie O'Brien). Only prosodic remark is that enclitic junctures allow pauses so a verb complex 'could consist of up to three phonological words' (p. 161).
sources.venue: The Non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Kamu (kmw), source Harvey 1990 'A sketch grammar of Gamu' (Dryer & Haspelmath eds.).
sources.note: No stress features: WALS CLDF values for kmw are only 51A, 81A-88A, 95A-97A, 143A-144B (case, word order, negation), all cited to Harvey 1990 pp. 32, 85, 94, passim; nothing for chapters 14-17.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1974. Daly Family Languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32. Canberra: ANU. Kamor = section 3b, pp. 62-68.
sources.note: Nothing. Kamor phonology (3b.2, pp. 62-63) is only 'a tentative list of Kamor phonemes' (consonants and vowels) noted as identical to Matngala and Yunggor; the whole 324-page volume has no statement on stress or accent for any Daly language (only 'it must be stressed'/'plurality is stressed' idioms).

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1968. The Daly River languages: a survey. In E. F. Aguas & D. T. Tryon (eds), Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3, 21-46. Pacific Linguistics A-14.
sources.note: Nothing; Kamor (language 5, Capell N.27) appears only in comparative wordlists; no phonological description.
No phonology at all; gives AIATSIS code N33 and extinction in the 1980s.

sources.note: The only published phonological description of Kamu; a syllabification study by the language's sole field linguist almost certainly states the stress pattern (stress and syllable structure are argued together in his other Top End work).
